title: Enterprise onboarding, integration, escalation and QBR playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended playbook for enterprise customer onboarding, integration checkpoints, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, and templates for regular health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE partners owning enterprise accounts.

Audience
--------
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers / Integration Engineers
- Support Engineers (L1/L2)
- Engineering on-call / SRE
- Account Executive and Renewal Owners (for QBRs)

Goals
-----
- Deliver predictable, low-friction onboarding for new enterprise customers
- Ensure timely resolution for escalations with clear SLAs and ownership
- Provide repeatable integration guidance and sample artifacts to accelerate time-to-value
- Maintain a standard set of health checks and QBR artifacts to surface risk and growth opportunities

Quick links
-----------
- Onboarding checklist (section)
- Integration guide and sample requests (section)
- Escalation matrix and runbook (section)
- Known issues & workarounds (section)
- Health checks & QBR template (section)

Pre-onboarding checklist (items required before kickoff)
----------------------------------------------------
| Item | Owner | Required by kickoff? | Notes |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Signed contract and billing contact | GTM | Yes | Include billing cadence, PO information if needed |
| IP allowlist & network peering details | Customer IT | Yes | Collect CIDRs, VPN / Direct Connect requirements |
| Model/data residency requirements | Customer Security | Yes | Determine whether Private deployment is required |
| Expected QPS and P95 latency targets | SE/CSM | Yes | Input to capacity planning / Dedicated sizing |
| Test dataset / sample prompts | Customer Product | Recommended | For quality baseline & evals |
| KMS/HSM and key rotation policy | Customer Security | Required for Private | Confirm supported KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) |

Onboarding phases and step-by-step runbook
----------------------------------------
1. Pre-kickoff (CSM + SE)
   - Confirm contract, billing, and SSO/Kerberos requirements.
   - Share pre-kickoff template with customer (network, IPs, expected traffic, credentials and contact matrix).
   - Create internal kickoff ticket: CS-<account>-onboard and link to Terraform / cloud account request if private/dedicated required.

2. Kickoff (Week 0)
   - Attendees: CSM, SE, Customer Technical Lead, Customer Security, Customer Product Owner.
   - Agenda: goals, timeline, security & compliance, integration approach (hosted vs dedicated vs private), rollout strategy, success metrics.
   - Deliverable: Agreed Project Plan with milestones and owners.

3. Integration & Validation (Week 1-3)
   - SE provides Integration Guide and SDK examples (see sample below).
   - Customer implements test calls against sandbox API / dedicated staging capacity.
   - Run baseline quality evals on sample prompts (document results).
   - Validate latency and error-rate SLOs against projected traffic patterns.

4. Security & Compliance Review (Week 2)
   - Exchange SOC2 evidence / architecture diagrams if required.
   - For Private deployments: coordinate on encryption, KMS, and audit logging configuration.

5. Pilot & Canary (Week 3-5)
   - Start with a limited production rollout (1-5% traffic).
   - Monitor KPIs: token cost, P95 latency, error-rate, throughput.
   - If regressions found, coordinate rollback or model variant fallback.

6. Full production ramp (Week 6+)
   - Gradually increase traffic as confidence grows; update SLOs and runbooks with observed baselines.
   - Schedule first 30/60/90 day QBR checkpoints.

Sample integration snippet (hosted API)
------------------------------------
Use the following examples in SE onboarding docs and SDK quickstarts. Replace <API_KEY> and <MODEL> before running.

Curl example:
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"<MODEL>","input":"Summarize our customer onboarding steps"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Node SDK example (pseudo)
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: '<MODEL>', input: 'Translate to French: Hello' });
console.log(res.output);

Integration checklist (common integrations to validate)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Authentication: API keys, SSO/OAuth (SAML or OIDC)
- Networking: IP allowlist, VPC peering, private endpoints for Private deployments
- Observability: Provide customer with route-level metrics and tracing hooks; validate log forwarding for Private
- Secrets: KMS integration, key provisioning, and rotation procedures
- Rate limiting and quotas: Confirm expected burst behavior and throttles

Escalation matrix and playbook
-----------------------------
Severity definitions and target response/next-step times: all times in business hours.
1) sev-1 (service down / production-critical)
   - Target: 15 min response (acknowledge), 1 hour workaround or mitigation, continuous updates every 30 minutes.
   - Primary owner: On-call SRE (pager) + SE escalation lead.
   - Actions:
     1. Triage in incident channel and create Incident in the tracker.
     2. If host-level, check Dedicated pool capacity and routing policies; if Hosted, validate regional fallbacks.
     3. If model-quality regression, activate fallback model variant and throttle non-critical traffic.

2) sev-2 (degraded performance, elevated error-rate)
   - Target: 1 hour response, mitigation in 4 hours.
   - Primary owner: Support L2 + SE.
   - Actions:
     1. Collect request IDs, sample payloads, and timestamps.
     2. Correlate with dashboard anomalies (token costs spike, latency P95 increase).
     3. If capacity-related, coordinate burst capacity request or temporary autoscale policy change.

3) sev-3 (feature request / non-urgent integration issue)
   - Target: 1 business day response, triage on next business day.
   - Primary owner: Support L1 / CSM.

--------------------------------

Escalation runbook: immediate steps (sev-1 / sev-2)
-------------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge within SLA and open incident page.
2. Capture customer-visible impact and affected routes/models.
3. If possible, apply short-term mitigation (e.g., model fallback, routing to other region, spin up burst capacity).
4. Triage logs and traces; notify customer with ETA and next update time.
5. Post-incident: run the incident review template and produce RCA within 5 business days.

Known issues and workarounds (living table)
-----------------------------------------
- Issue: Intermittent 503s when requests contain very large prompt prefixes
  Workaround: Enforce prefix truncation in client SDKs. For customers on Dedicated, raise request to increase allowed sequence length; enable prefix caching to reduce repeated KV eviction.

- Issue: Higher than expected token cost for bursty workloads with many short requests
  Workaround: Recommend batch-assisted client (SDK option) and encourage using a rewriter/aggregation layer to combine small requests. Suggest enabling short-lived caching at gateway.

- Issue: SAML assertion misconfiguration causing SSO login failures
  Workaround: Confirm Audience URI and ACS URLs; provide SAML metadata file and IdP mapping examples.

- Issue: Private deployment image fails at start on air-gapped customers due to missing kernel modules
  Workaround: Provide the exact kernel module list and preflight script; offer a remote engineering session to patch the host or provide prebuilt VM image.

Health checks and monitoring checklist (weekly)
---------------------------------------------
- Service-level KPIs to surface at weekly health checks:
  - P95 latency (target < 200ms for tier-1 customers on Dedicated)
  - Error rate (5xx) < 0.1% over rolling 24h window
  - Token cost per 1k tokens vs expected baseline (variance < \u00b115%)
  - Throughput vs provisioned capacity (utilization < 80% for predictable headroom)
- Operational checks:
  - Verify audit logs forwarding for Private deployments
  - Confirm alerts: SLO burn, degraded model quality, capacity saturation
  - Validate backups and snapshot cadence for model artifacts (if customer-managed)

QBR template and agenda (30-60 minute cadence)
---------------------------------------------
1. Executive summary (5 min) \u2014 adoption, ARR activity, and top outcomes
2. Adoption metrics (10 min) \u2014 total calls, unique users, growth vs prior quarter
3. Reliability and performance (10 min) \u2014 SLOs, incidents, availability, actions taken
4. Cost and optimization (5-10 min) \u2014 token spend, batching/quantization opportunities, projected optimizations
5. Roadmap and ask (5 min) \u2014 feature requests, model onboarding, scaling needs
6. Action items and owners (5 min) \u2014 next steps and timelines

QBR artifacts to prepare (pre-call)
- One-page adoption dashboard (png/pdf)
- Incident summary since last QBR (R/Y/G status per incident)
- Cost delta and optimization proposals (spreadsheet)
- Open action items tracker (tickets and owners)

Escalation and postmortem timelines
----------------------------------
- Incident acknowledgement: within SLA (see matrix).
- Initial incident summary to customer: within 2 hours for sev-1, 8 hours for sev-2.
- Postmortem delivered (RCA): within 5 business days for sev-1, 10 business days for sev-2.

Ownership & metrics (who does what)
----------------------------------
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall customer relationship, QBR owner, adoption metrics.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration lead, technical design, POC support.
- Support L1/L2: first-line triage, initial remediation, ticket routing.
- SRE / Runtime Eng: production reliability, capacity, and incident response.
- Product / Model Ops: model-quality regressions triage and variant rollouts.

Appendix: useful commands and artifacts
-------------------------------------
- Retrieve recent request logs (CLI example):
  redwood-cli logs tail --account <acct-id> --from 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-03-04T00:00:00Z --filter "status>=500"

- Example JSON to start a canary rollout:
  {
    "route_id": "customer-acct-123",
    "policy": {
      "canary_percentage": 5,
      "model_variant": "gptx-1-small"
    }
  }

- Contact matrix (operational)
  - On-call: oncall+redwood-sre@redwood.ai (PagerDuty)
  - SE escalation: se-esc@redwood.ai (Slack #se-escalations)
  - Support portal: support.redwood.ai/tickets
